subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: What delivery contract should the SMS webhook use when a signature-validated callback exceeds the accepted-callback quota: reject it for retry/fallback, durably queue it before acknowledging, or deliberately acknowledge and discard it?
rationale: All three policies have different message-loss, overload, and operator-observability consequences, and current repository behavior does not establish that a callback may be reported successful without being accepted.

options.title: Preserve failure semantics
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 for unaccepted callbacks and document Twilio `rp=4xx` or fallback configuration until OpenClaw has durable admission.

options.title: Queue before acknowledging
options.body: Add a bounded durable callback queue and return HTTP 200 only after the message has been accepted for later dispatch.

options.title: Own ack-and-drop
options.body: Explicitly adopt intentional loss under overload with clear documentation, metrics, logs, and maintainer acceptance that Twilio will record success.

recommendation.title: Preserve failure semantics
recommendation.body: Keep HTTP 429 for unaccepted callbacks and document Twilio `rp=4xx` or fallback configuration until OpenClaw has durable admission.
